title: What Is Amazon KDP? Kindle Direct Publishing Explained for New Authors
excerpt: KDP stands for Kindle Direct Publishing, Amazon's free platform to self-publish ebooks and paperbacks. This guide explains how it works: royalties, pricing, ISBNs, KDP Select and the most common first-upload mistakes.

html:
KDP stands for Kindle Direct Publishing, Amazon's free platform to self-publish ebooks and paperbacks (and hardcovers). You upload your manuscript and cover, set a price, and Amazon sells your book and pays you a royalty on each sale.

There's no fee to publish, and you don't need a literary agent or a publisher. You keep the rights to your book, set your own price, and can update or unpublish it later. KDP is not a publisher, though: Amazon doesn't edit or promote your book, and it doesn't guarantee sales.

This guide explains how KDP works for first-time authors: ebook and paperback publishing, royalties, pricing, ISBNs, KDP Select, and the most common mistakes on a first upload. Figures are taken from KDP's own help pages.

How Amazon KDP Works

  1. Create a KDP account at kdp.amazon.com using your Amazon account. Complete your tax information during setup.
  2. Start a new title — Click "Create" on your Bookshelf and choose Kindle eBook, Paperback or Hardcover.
  3. Enter book details — Title, author, description, categories and keywords.
  4. Upload manuscript and cover — Use KDP's previewer to check chapter breaks, the table of contents and any images before you continue.
  5. Set your price and royalty option — KDP shows your estimated royalty per sale as you enter a price.
  6. Publish — KDP reviews the book. Ebooks go live in up to 3 business days. Paperback detail pages appear in up to 72 hours on Amazon.com and up to 5 days on other marketplaces.

Once the book is live, Amazon handles sales and delivery. Print copies are printed only when a customer orders one. Royalties are paid monthly, about 60 days after the end of the month in which they were earned, once you reach the payment threshold. You can change the book after publishing: KDP says a price change takes about 24 hours, and changes to the description, keywords, manuscript or cover can take up to 72 hours.

Ebook Publishing on KDP

Your ebook is listed in the Kindle Store and can be read on Kindle devices and in the Kindle app on phones, tablets and computers. KDP converts your uploaded file to Kindle format.

KDP's suggested ebook formats are Word (DOC/DOCX), EPUB and KPF, the file made by Amazon's free Kindle Create tool. KDP also accepts HTML, RTF and TXT, and PDF for some languages only. Whatever you upload, check the result in Kindle Previewer before you publish.

Paperback Publishing on KDP

Your paperback or hardcover is printed only when a customer orders it. You never hold inventory. If your interior has images that bleed to the page edge, you must upload it as a PDF. Without bleed, KDP also accepts DOC, DOCX, RTF, HTML or TXT and converts the file to PDF. The cover is a single PDF (back, spine and front) sized for your trim size and page count, or you can build one with KDP's Cover Creator. The KDP paperback cover specs list bleed, spine and PDF requirements.

Each print format needs its own ISBN (see below). Deciding between ebook only and ebook plus paperback? The KDP print vs digital guide compares formats, royalties and distribution.

How KDP Royalties Work

Two royalty options for ebooks:

  • 70% royalty — For ebooks with a list price from $2.99 to $12.99 on Amazon.com. KDP raised the top of this band from $9.99 to $12.99 on July 7, 2026. A delivery cost based on file size is subtracted first ($0.15 per MB on Amazon.com). A $4.99 ebook earns roughly $3.49 per sale before that delivery cost.
  • 35% royalty — Applies outside that price band, and to sales to customers outside KDP's 70% territories. In Brazil, Japan, Mexico and India, an ebook earns 70% only if it is enrolled in KDP Select and meets the price requirements there; otherwise it earns 35%.

Paperback royalty on Amazon.com is 60% of the list price at $9.99 or above, or 50% at $9.98 or below, minus the printing cost. A $12.99 paperback with a $3.50 printing cost earns approximately $4.29 per sale (0.60 × $12.99 − $3.50). Sales through Expanded Distribution earn 40% minus printing. Printing cost depends on trim size, page count, ink and marketplace; KDP's royalty calculator shows your exact figure before you publish.

Pricing Your KDP Book

Your ebook price decides your royalty option. To get 70% on Amazon.com, the list price must sit between $2.99 and $12.99. Below or above that, you earn 35%. The 35% option also has a minimum price that rises with file size. KDP lists the bands for every marketplace on its eBook List Price Requirements page.

For a paperback, the price decides the royalty rate (50% or 60% on Amazon.com), and the printing cost comes off the top. Run the numbers in KDP's royalty calculator before you pick a price. For strategy — launch pricing, genre norms and when to discount — see the KDP ebook pricing guide.

Do You Need an ISBN for KDP?

Not for an ebook. KDP says ISBNs are optional for ebooks, and Amazon identifies your Kindle edition with its own ASIN.

Paperbacks and hardcovers do need one, and each format needs its own ISBN. KDP offers a free ISBN for paperbacks and hardcovers. Two catches: a free KDP ISBN can only be used on KDP, and the imprint shows as "Independently published". If you want to publish the same edition elsewhere, or under your own imprint, buy your own ISBN.

What You Need Before Publishing

  • Finished, edited manuscript
  • Ebook cover image: JPEG or TIFF, under 50MB. KDP's ideal size is 2,560 × 1,600 pixels (height × width); the minimum is 1,000 × 625.
  • Book description (your Amazon product page blurb)
  • Up to 3 categories, chosen from KDP's own category list
  • Up to 7 keywords or short phrases (optional)
  • An answer on AI: KDP requires you to disclose AI-generated content (text, images or translations)
  • Tax info and bank account for royalty payments

Formatting Your Book for KDP

File formatting is where many first-time authors get stuck. A file that doesn't convert cleanly can fail at upload, or go through and look wrong in the Kindle preview.

Common structural problems in exported EPUB files include:

  • Missing or malformed table of contents
  • EPUB package structure errors (missing OPF file, broken manifest)
  • XHTML files that don't validate
  • Images referenced in the HTML but not included in the EPUB package
  • Metadata errors (missing language, missing title)

These can come from exporting straight from Word or converting with Calibre without checking the output. Before you upload, run the file through the free EPUB Validator and preview it in Kindle Previewer.

For the full process — manuscript preparation, headings, chapter breaks, the table of contents, images and a pre-upload checklist — follow the KDP formatting guide.

If you've already been rejected by KDP, these guides cover the most common specific errors:

  • KDP "No TOC Found" error — what it means and how to fix it
  • Common EPUB validation errors and how to resolve them

If you're formatting a book for the first time, this step-by-step guide covers the full formatting process from raw manuscript to validated EPUB at zero cost.

KDP Select: Is It Worth It?

During setup, KDP will ask whether you want to enroll in KDP Select. This is optional — and understanding it before you decide matters.

What KDP Select gives you:

  • Your book is included in Kindle Unlimited — Amazon's subscription service where readers pay a monthly fee to read as many books as they want. You earn a share of the monthly KDP Select Global Fund based on pages read (KENP). The per-page amount changes each month.
  • Access to promotional tools: up to 5 free promotion days per 90-day enrollment period, and Kindle Countdown Deals (Amazon.com and Amazon.co.uk only).
  • 70% royalties on sales in Brazil, Japan, Mexico and India, if your price meets the requirements there.

What KDP Select requires:

  • Exclusivity — While enrolled, the digital edition of your book can only be distributed through KDP. You cannot sell it on Apple Books, Kobo, Barnes & Noble, or anywhere else, including your own website. Your paperback is not affected.
  • 90-day enrollment periods — Enrollment runs in 90-day periods. Check your enrollment settings on your KDP Bookshelf before a period ends if you plan to leave.

Whether Select is worth it depends on how many of your readers use Kindle Unlimited, and whether you want to sell the ebook in other stores. You can publish without it and enroll later.

Common Mistakes First-Time KDP Authors Make

  • Uploading a file that was never checked. Exports from Word or Calibre can carry TOC and package errors. Validate first, then preview in Kindle Previewer.
  • Using the wrong cover size or format. The ebook cover is a JPEG or TIFF, ideally 2,560 × 1,600 pixels. A print cover is a different file: one PDF with back, spine and front.
  • Pricing outside the 70% band by accident. On Amazon.com, an ebook priced below $2.99 or above $12.99 earns 35%.
  • Enrolling in KDP Select while selling the ebook elsewhere. Select requires digital exclusivity, including your own website.
  • Taking the free ISBN without reading the terms. A free KDP ISBN can only be used on KDP.
  • Fake headings and manual spacing. Bold text instead of heading styles, and extra Returns instead of page breaks, can break the Kindle TOC and layout.

For the formatting side in more detail, see common Kindle formatting mistakes.

KDP vs. Traditional Publishing

KDPTraditional Publishing
Time to publishDaysOften a year or more
Royalty rate35% or 70% (ebook); 50% or 60% minus printing (paperback)A lower share of list price, set by contract
AdvanceNoneVaries by publisher and contract
Editorial supportSelf-arrangedIncluded
RightsYou keep themLicensed to publisher

The two paths aren't mutually exclusive, and some authors use both.

Get Your Files Ready Before You Upload

Three free checks before your first upload:

  • EPUB Validator — checks your EPUB's structure in your browser and explains each error in plain English.
  • Cover Checker — checks your ebook cover's dimensions and file format against KDP's cover guidelines.
  • KDP Preflight Checklist — a pre-upload checklist based on KDP's help pages.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does it cost to publish on Amazon KDP?

Nothing. KDP doesn't charge to publish or update a book. Amazon keeps part of each sale as its share, and for print books the printing cost is deducted from your royalty.

How long does it take for a KDP book to go live?

Ebooks go live in up to 3 business days after you publish. Paperback detail pages appear in up to 72 hours on Amazon.com and up to 5 days on other marketplaces.

Can I sell my book elsewhere if I publish on KDP?

Yes, unless you're enrolled in KDP Select. Without KDP Select, you can sell the same ebook on Apple Books, Kobo, Barnes & Noble, Google Play, and your own website simultaneously.

What's the difference between KDP and Kindle Unlimited?

KDP is the publishing platform — how you get your book onto Amazon. Kindle Unlimited is a reader subscription service. Enrolling in KDP Select makes your book available in Kindle Unlimited. You can publish on KDP without enrolling in either KDP Select or Kindle Unlimited.

Why does KDP reject EPUB files?

Structural problems in the file — a missing or malformed table of contents, a broken OPF manifest, invalid XHTML or images that aren't packaged — can stop an EPUB from converting cleanly. Check your EPUB with a validator before uploading. See KDP rejecting your EPUB file for a full breakdown of causes and fixes.

Do I need an ISBN to publish on KDP?

Not for an ebook — KDP says ISBNs are optional for ebooks, and Amazon assigns its own ASIN. Paperbacks and hardcovers need an ISBN, one per format. KDP offers a free one for print books, but it can only be used on KDP.
